timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Below is a practical workflow you can follow to find a short‑running film (≤ 2 h) that’s showing at a theater close to Times Square. Because there isn’t a single “public” API that gives you *both* the runtime AND the exact showtimes for a given theater, the trick is to combine two services: | Step | What you’ll do | Why it works | |------|----------------|--------------| | 1 | Query **The Movie Database (TMDb)** for all films that are currently “Now Playing” in the United States. | TMDb offers a free, well‑documented REST API that returns each movie’s runtime, title, release date, poster, etc. | | 2 | Filter that list locally for movies whose `runtime` ≤ 120 minutes. | That guarantees the film itself is short enough. | | 3 | Pick a theater that’s literally next to Times Square – the most popular ones are
• **AMC Empire 25** (address: 234 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036)
• **Regal Broadway Cinemas** (address: 226 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036) | Both are within a 5‑minute walk from Times Square. | | 4 | Visit the theater’s own website (or use a service like Fandango) to pull the current showtimes for the filtered movies. | Theater sites publish real‑time schedules; Fandango aggregates them and has its own API (though it usually needs an API key). | --- ## 1️⃣ Get the list of short movies with TMDb ```python import requests API_KEY = "YOUR_TMDB_API_KEY" # <-- put your key here BASE_URL = "https://api.themoviedb.org/3" def get_now_playing_us(): url = f"{BASE_URL}/movie/now_playing" params = { "api_key": API_KEY, "language": "en-US", "region": "US", # restrict to U.S. releases "page": 1 # start with page 1 } resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=10) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json()["results"] def filter_short_movies(movies, max_runtime=120): """Return only those movies whose runtime is <= max_runtime.""" short = [] for m in movies: # Some entries don’t include runtime in the “now_playing” payload. # We’ll fetch the full details for those that do. if m.get("runtime") is None: detail_url = f"{BASE_URL}/movie/{m['id']}" detail_resp = requests.get(detail_url, params={"api_key": API_KEY}, timeout=10) detail_resp.raise_for_status() m.update(detail_resp.json()) if m["runtime"] <= max_runtime: short.append({ "title": m["title"], "runtime": m["runtime"], "release_date": m["release_date"], "overview": m["overview"] }) return short movies = get_now_playing_us() short_movies = filter_short_movies(movies) print(f"Found {len(short_movies)} short movies:") for i, m in enumerate(short_movies[:10], 1): # show first 10 print(f"{i}. {m['title']} ({m['runtime']} min) – released {m['release_date']}") ``` > **Tip:** You can paginate through all pages (`page=2`, `page=3`, …) until `total_pages` is reached. > The above snippet only pulls page 1 for brevity. --- ## 2️⃣ Check the showtimes at a nearby theater ### Option A – Directly on the theater’s site Both AMC Empire 25 and Regal Broadway Cinemas have a “Showtimes” page that lists every film and its times for the week. If you’re comfortable with a quick manual lookup, just open: * **AMC Empire 25** → https://www.amctheatres.com/movie-theaters/new-york-city/amc-empire-25/showtimes * **Regal Broadway Cinemas** → https://www.regmovies.com/theater/regal-broadway-cinemas Then scroll down to the “Now Showing” section and look for any of the titles you pulled from TMDb. ### Option B – Using Fandango’s (unofficial) API Fandango publishes showtimes on a per‑theater basis.
